info.title: Patch My PC Cloud Customer API
info.description: The Patch My PC Cloud Customer API lets you search and manage your applications, deployments, and deployment templates. Every operation except the token exchange requires an access token.

servers.description: United States. Use this host if your Patch My PC account is in the US region.
Europe. Use this host if your Patch My PC account is in the EU region.

post.description: Completes a new application creation process.

schema.description:
Completes a draft to create a custom application, add a new version to one, or edit one in place.
When adding a new version, only version-level fields are used; application-level fields such as
`displayName`, `description`, `publisher`, `language` and the URLs are ignored.

put.description: Completes an in-place edit of an existing custom application version. Changes product metadata (display name, description, publisher, owner, developer, icon, and URLs) and update-level settings without creating a new version.

When adding a new version, only version-level fields are used; application-level fields such as

post.description: Creates a draft for editing an existing version of a custom application in place. Unlike an update draft, this doesn't create a new version—it opens the existing version for revision, so you can correct metadata without publishing a new version number.

schema.description:
Identifies the application to open a draft for: an update draft for a new version, or an edit draft

post.description: Searches your own custom applications. Any feed types in the request body are ignored and replaced with `CUSTOMER`.

schema.description: Search criteria for the application search endpoints. All filters are optional.

post.description: Creates a new update draft for an existing custom application.

schema.description:
Identifies the application to open a draft for: an update draft for a new version, or an edit draft
for an existing version.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in your custom application catalog. Returns only the fields relevant to a custom application.

delete.description: Deletes a custom application you own, freeing a slot against your custom application limit. Only your own custom applications can be deleted; public catalog applications are shared and can't be deleted. The request is rejected while the application's latest update is in a state that isn't safe to remove.

put.description: Completes an in-place edit of an existing application version. Changes product metadata (display name, description, publisher, owner, developer, icon, and URLs) and update-level settings without creating a new version. To publish a new version instead, use `PUT /v1/api/apps/complete`.

schema.description:
Completes a draft to create a custom application, add a new version to one, or edit one in place.
When adding a new version, only version-level fields are used; application-level fields such as
`displayName`, `description`, `publisher`, `language` and the URLs are ignored.

post.description: Creates a draft for editing an existing version of an application in place. Unlike an update draft, this doesn't create a new version—it opens the existing version for revision, so you can correct metadata without publishing a new version number.

schema.description:
Identifies the application to open a draft for: an update draft for a new version, or an edit draft

post.description: Searches the public Patch My PC catalog. Results describe the architecture, language, installer type and install context options for the requested operating system; not every combination can be deployed, so use the application details to see the exact variants. Any feed types in the request body are ignored and replaced with `PMPC`. `connectionId` is required and identifies the Intune connection that scopes the search.

schema.description: Search criteria for the application search endpoints. All filters are optional.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in the public Patch My PC catalog, including the variants you can deploy for the requested operating system. Each variant has a `catalogEntryId` that identifies your selection when you create a deployment. `connectionId` is required and identifies the Intune connection that scopes the lookup. `osType` is optional and defaults to `Windows`; `MacOS` requires your account to be entitled to macOS applications, otherwise the application is reported as not found.

post.description: Searches your custom applications using advanced filtering options. Any feed types in the request are ignored and replaced with `CUSTOMER`.

schema.description: Search criteria for the application search endpoints. All filters are optional.

post.description: Creates a new update draft for an existing application.

schema.description:
Identifies the application to open a draft for: an update draft for a new version, or an edit draft
for an existing version.

get.description: Retrieves detailed information about an application in your custom application catalog by its product ID.

delete.description: Deletes a custom application you own, freeing a slot against your custom application limit. Only your own custom applications can be deleted; public catalog applications are shared and can't be deleted. The request is rejected while the application's latest update is in a state that isn't safe to remove.

get.description: Lists the Intune deployments that exist for an application under the given connection.

post.description: Creates a new Intune deployment. Both custom and public applications require CatalogEntryId from details, identifying an entry for the route's product, connection and operating system. Public applications require an explicit variant selection. The broker resolves current deployment metadata without historical fallback or version pinning.

schema.description:
Request body to create an Intune deployment for an application. The application is identified by the
`productId` in the route. The deployment's display name is taken from the application's name, with a
number appended if that name is already used in the connection.

get.description: Lists the existing deployments in the given connection that you can pick as a dependency for a new or edited deployment. Every deployment in the connection is returned; filter the results on the client.

Retrieves full detail for a single Intune deployment, including categories, Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles, and the dependency chain (parent and child deployments)—fields that the list operation doesn't return.

put.description: Edits an existing Intune deployment's name, group assignments, categories, ESP profiles, dependencies, and configuration—conflicting-process behavior, return codes, requirements, install parameters, application information overrides, and behavior settings. Any field you leave unset keeps its current value. Not supported for ring-enabled deployments.

schema.description:
Request body to edit an existing Intune deployment. The deployment is identified by the `deploymentId`
in the route. All fields except `connectionId` are optional; an omitted field keeps its current value.
Ring-enabled deployments cannot be edited, and settings this request does not include, such as rings, custom
scripts and extra files, are always kept unchanged.

delete.description: Deletes an existing Intune deployment. Allowed only while the deployment isn't in progress or already being deleted.

put.description: Forces a deployment to be recreated in Intune. Use it to troubleshoot a stuck or corrupted deployment; for routine version updates, use the sync operation instead.

put.summary: Set application deployment sync pause status
put.description: Pauses or resumes a deployment's scheduled sync.

schema.description:
Request body to pause or resume a deployment's scheduled sync. The deployment is identified by the
`deploymentId` in the route.

put.description: Syncs a deployment to its latest pending version. Use it for routine version updates; to troubleshoot a stuck or corrupted deployment, use the redeploy operation instead.

get.description: Lists the files of an application's current version, in exactly the shape the completion operations accept. An edit replaces the file list rather than merging it, so you must send the complete list back; use this operation to get it without rebuilding it from local state.

post.summary: Exchange a personal access token for an access token
post.description: Exchanges a personal access token, supplied in the `Authorization` header as a bearer credential, for an access token that's valid for 60 minutes. Send the access token on subsequent requests, and exchange the personal access token again when the access token expires.

get.description: Lists the Intune connections available to the selected company. Use a connection's ID to scope application and deployment operations.
Retrieves information about your customer account, including its license and usage limits.

Lists the deployment templates configured for a connection, so you can find one and name it when you create a deployment. To author and change templates, use the create, update, and delete deployment template operations.

post.description: Creates a deployment template on a connection. Setting it as the default demotes the template that's currently the default.

schema.description:
The settings to store on a deployment template. When updating a template, every field is stored as sent, so
get the template first and change only what you need.

get.description: Retrieves the settings that a deployment created from this template inherits.

put.description: Replaces the settings on an existing deployment template. Every field is stored as sent, so read the template first and change only what you need.

schema.description:
The settings to store on a deployment template. When updating a template, every field is stored as sent, so
get the template first and change only what you need.

delete.description: Deletes a deployment template. You can't delete the connection's default template—make another template the default first.

requirementArchitecture.description: The processor architecture a device must have to install the application.

architecture.description:
Which registry architecture to search when detecting the installed application by its
Add/Remove Programs (ARP) entry. `TargetDefault` searches all architectures.

arpDisplayNameMatch.description:
A pattern that matches the application's display name in Add/Remove Programs (ARP), used to
detect whether the application is installed. Required when creating an application.

arpVersionMatch.description:
The version of the application this draft publishes, as shown in its Add/Remove Programs (ARP)
entry. Returned as `updateVersion` in the application details.

conflictingProcesses.description: The names of processes that conflict with installing the application.

displayName.description: The application's display name. Required when creating or editing an application.

documentationURL.description:
The URL of the application's documentation. Optional, and used only when creating an
application.

privacyURL.description: The URL of the application's privacy policy. Optional.

informationURL.description: The URL of a web page with more information about the application. Optional.

installContext.description: The context the application installs in, for example `System` or `User`.

language.description: The application's language code, for example `en-US`.

intuneNotes.description: Notes to include with the application in Microsoft Intune. Optional.

publisher.description:
The name of the application's publisher. Required when creating or editing an application.
It is matched against your existing publishers ignoring case, and a new publisher is created
if none matches.

updateId.description: The ID of the version (update) to complete, as returned by the draft endpoint. Required.

productId.description:
The application's ID, as returned by the draft endpoint. Required when adding a new version or
editing an application.

msiProductCode.description:
The MSI product code (a GUID) of the application's installer. When set, the application is
treated as an MSI installer; when `null`, it is treated as an EXE installer.

detectionRules.description:
Custom rules that detect whether the application is installed. When `null`, detection is
based on `msiProductCode`, `arpDisplayNameMatch` and `arpVersionMatch`.

customRequirements.description:
Custom requirement rules a device must meet before the application installs. When `null`,
requirements are based on `requirementArchitecture` only.

revisionId.description: The revision ID returned by the draft endpoint.

iconUrl.description: The key of an uploaded icon file to use as the application's icon. Optional.

folderPath.description:
The local folder that contains the application's files. Optional and informational only: the
file paths in `files` and `primaryInstallerFile` are relative to this folder.

primaryInstallerFile.description:
The path of the main installer file, relative to the application folder. Backslashes are
converted to forward slashes, and the path is matched against the `fileName` values in
`files`, ignoring case.

cmdArguments.description:
The command-line arguments used to install the application silently. For an MSI installer,
these are used as the MSI command line.

files.description:
Every file in the application version, including the main installer. When editing, this list
replaces the existing files, so send the complete list. Requests that include restricted file
names are rejected.

silentUninstallArg.description: The command-line arguments used to uninstall the application silently. Optional.

ApplicationCompletionRequest.description:
Completes a draft to create a custom application, add a new version to one, or edit one in place.
When adding a new version, only version-level fields are used; application-level fields such as
`displayName`, `description`, `publisher`, `language` and the URLs are ignored.

updateId.description:
The ID of the application version (update) the draft or operation applies to. Pass it to the
completion endpoint as `updateId`.

revisionId.description: The revision ID of the draft. Pass it to the completion endpoint as `revisionId`.

displayName.description: The application's display name. Empty in draft responses.

customerId.description:
The ID of the customer account that owns the application. Set when an operation completes;
draft responses return an empty GUID.

fileUploadPath.description:
The relative API path for uploading a small file in a single multipart/form-data request.
Returned only in draft responses.

chunkedFileUploadPath.description: The relative API path for uploading a large file in chunks. Returned only in draft responses.

fileCompleteUploadPath.description: The relative API path for completing a chunked file upload. Returned only in draft responses.

ApplicationCreationResponse.description:
Returned when you create a draft, or complete an application create, update or edit. Draft
responses also include the paths for uploading the application's files.

productId.description:
The ID of the application the file belongs to. Ignored when you send the file in a completion
request.

fileName.description: The file's path relative to the application folder, using forward slashes (`/`).

fileType.description:
The file's role in the application, for example `Installation` for the main installer or
`Extra` for a supporting file.

sha1Hash.description: The SHA-1 hash of the file contents, as a hexadecimal string.

sha256Hash.description:
The SHA-256 hash of the file contents, as a hexadecimal string. Only the main installer file
(`Installation`) uses it; for other files it is `null` in responses and ignored in
requests.

ApplicationFileDto.description:
A file in an application version. The application files endpoint returns files in this shape, and
the completion endpoints accept the same shape in `files`.

productId.description: The ID of the application to create the draft for.

updateId.description:
The ID of the version (update) to edit. Used only when creating an edit draft; ignored for an
update draft.

ApplicationUpdateDraftRequest.description:
Identifies the application to open a draft for: an update draft for a new version, or an edit draft
for an existing version.

connectionId.description: Unique ID of the connection. Pass it as the connection for deployment operations.

displayName.description: Display name of the connection, or `null` if none is set.

type.description: The connection type. Only Intune connections are returned.

adminConsent.description:
The admin consent status of the connection, such as `Granted`, `Pending` or
`MissingPermissions`.

ConnectionDto.description:
An Intune connection available to the selected company. Use `connectionId` to choose the
connection that deployment operations run against.

groupId.description:
Microsoft Entra ID group ID, from your own tenant, to assign the deployment to. Required when
`targetType` is `Group` (or omitted) and `intent` is `Required`, `Available`,
`Uninstall` or `UpdateOnly`. Optional for `AvailableWithoutEnrollment`. Must be omitted for
every other target type and for the no-assignment intents. To target all users or all devices, set
`targetType` instead of passing a group ID.

intent.description:
What Intune does with the app for this assignment, for example `Required`, `Available`,
`Uninstall` or `UpdateOnly`. `Unknown` is not accepted. The no-assignment intents,
`NoAssignmentsInstall` and `NoAssignmentsUpdate`, create a deployment that is assigned to nobody.
For those, omit `targetType` (or set it to `NotSet`) and `groupId`; any other value is
rejected with a 400 response.

targetType.description:
Who the assignment targets. `Group` targets the group in `groupId`. `AllUsers` and
`AllDevices` target the whole tenant and must not include a `groupId`. `NotSet` is valid
only with the no-assignment intents. When omitted, the assignment targets a group, except with the
no-assignment intents, where it targets nobody.

CreateDeploymentAssignmentRequest.description:
A single Intune assignment for a deployment. Pairs an `intent` (what Intune does with the app for the
target) with a `targetType` (who the target is). The combination must be valid, or the request is
rejected with a 400 response.

connectionId.description: ID of the Intune connection (tenant) to create the deployment under. Required.

osType.description: Operating system the deployment targets, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

catalogEntryId.description:
Selects the exact catalog entry to deploy, for a custom or public application. Required. Use the entry ID
from the application's details for this operating system. It identifies a recipe, not a pinned version or
revision.

assignments.description: Assignments for the deployment: who it targets and with what intent. At least one assignment is required.

categoryIds.description:
IDs of the Intune categories to assign to the deployment. Omit, or send an empty list, to assign no
categories.

espProfileIds.description:
IDs of the Intune Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles to assign to the deployment. Omit, or send an empty
list, to assign none. There is no endpoint to list ESP profiles, so get the profile ID from the Intune admin
center.

parentDeploymentIds.description:
IDs of existing deployments this deployment depends on. Those deployments must finish installing first.
Omit, or send an empty list, for no dependencies. Use the dependency candidates endpoint to find eligible
deployments.

configuration.description:
Optional deployment configuration: conflicting-process behavior, return codes, requirements, install
parameters, app information overrides and behavior settings. Omit it to create the deployment with
default settings.

CreateDeploymentRequest.description:
Request body to create an Intune deployment for an application. The application is identified by the
`productId` in the route. The deployment's display name is taken from the application's name, with a
number appended if that name is already used in the connection.

productId.description:
The ID of the application this entry belongs to. Included in application details; omitted from
search results.

catalogEntryId.description:
The ID of the catalog entry for this custom application. Pass it as `catalogEntryId` when you
create a deployment. Omitted from search results and when the entry ID is not available.

updateId.description:
The ID of the update associated with this custom application. Included in search and detail
responses when available. It is not necessarily the update for the version shown in the result.

CustomApplicationDetailsDto.description:
Details specific to a custom application. Custom applications are the only type you can create,
update, edit and delete.

type.description:
The application type: `pmpc` for a Patch My PC catalog application, or `custom` for
one of your custom applications.

language.description: The application's language code, for example `en-US`.

vendorName.description: The name of the application's publisher (vendor).

updateVersion.description: The version number of the application's latest version.

iconURL.description:
A reference to the application's icon file. This is a key, not a download link; the icon image
itself is returned in `iconBase64`.

iconBase64.description:
The application's icon image, Base64-encoded. `null` when the application has no icon or
the icon could not be retrieved.

iconContentType.description:
The MIME type of the icon in `iconBase64`, for example `image/png`. Set only when
`iconBase64` is set.

privacyUrl.description: The URL of the application's privacy policy.

informationUrl.description: The URL of a web page with more information about the application.

intuneNotes.description: Notes to include with the application in Microsoft Intune.

installerType.description: The type of installer the application uses, for example `MSI` or `EXE`.

architecture.description: The processor architecture a device must have to install the application.

installContext.description: The context the application installs in, for example `System` or `User`.

actions.description:
The actions you can currently perform on this application. A custom application allows
`deploy`, `update`, `edit`, `delete` and `download-files`; a Patch My
PC catalog application allows `deploy` only.

custom.description:
Identity details of this custom application, including the catalog entry ID needed to create a
deployment. Omitted when not available.

silentInstallArguments.description:
The command-line arguments used to install the application silently. For an MSI installer,
this is the MSI command line.

silentUninstallArguments.description: The command-line arguments used to uninstall the application silently.

mainFile.description: The file name of the application's main installer file.

conflictingProcessList.description: The names of processes that conflict with installing the application.

detectionRules.description:
Custom rules that detect whether the application is installed. `null` when none are set,
in which case detection is based on `msiProductCode` or `arpDisplayNameMatch`.

customRequirements.description: Custom requirement rules a device must meet before the application installs.

arpDisplayNameMatch.description:
A pattern that matches the application's display name in Add/Remove Programs (ARP), used to
detect whether the application is installed.

msiProductCode.description:
The MSI product code (a GUID) of the application's installer. `null` when the installer is
not an MSI.

isMigrationApp.description:
Whether the application was migrated from another source rather than created directly as a
custom application. `null` when the value is not available.

CustomApplicationDto.description:
Details of one of your custom applications, returned by `GET /apps/custom/{productId}`.
Includes the installation settings, which you manage for a custom application.

applicableArchitectures.description:
Windows architectures the application can install on. When empty, the single architecture in
`requirementArchitecture` applies.

minimumWindowsOSVersion.description: Minimum Windows version the device must run. `null` when no minimum is set.

minimumNumberOfProcessors.description: Minimum number of logical processors the device must have.

minimumMemoryInMB.description: Minimum amount of physical memory the device must have, in MB.

minimumCpuSpeedInMHz.description: Minimum processor speed the device must have, in MHz.

requirementFileRules.description: File and folder requirement rules. Every rule must pass before the application installs.

requirementRegistryRules.description: Registry requirement rules. Every rule must pass before the application installs.

requirementsScriptRules.description: Script requirement rules. Every rule must pass before the application installs.

CustomRequirementsDto.description:
Requirement rules a device must meet before the application installs. If you omit these on a
create or update request, the only requirement applied is the architecture in `requirementArchitecture`.

limits.description:
The limits that apply to the customer's account, such as the maximum number of custom
applications, the maximum size of a single custom application and the total storage allowed.

license.description: Details of the customer's Patch My PC license.

limitsProgress.description:
The customer's current usage of their custom applications, such as the number of custom
applications and the storage they use. Compare these values with `limits`.

macOSApplicationsEnabled.description:
Whether the customer has access to macOS applications. When `false`, macOS applications are
not returned, so an empty macOS result does not mean that no applications matched.

CustomerInfoDto.description:
Account information for the customer the caller is signed in to, including license details,
account limits and current usage against those limits.

customVendor.description: Publisher name shown in the Company Portal.

customDeveloper.description: Developer name shown in the Company Portal.

customOwner.description: Owner shown in the Company Portal.

customDescription.description: Description shown in the Company Portal.

customNotes.description: Free-text notes shown in the Company Portal.

customInformationUrl.description: Information URL shown in the Company Portal.

customPrivacyUrl.description: Privacy statement URL shown in the Company Portal.

isFeatured.description:
Whether the application is shown as a featured app in the Company Portal. When omitted on create, the
application is not featured.

DeploymentAppInfoDto.description:
Overrides for the application information shown in the Intune Company Portal. Each override applies to this
deployment only and does not change the application in the catalog. When reading a deployment, a
`null` field is not overridden and the catalog value is used. When creating a deployment, omit a field
to use the catalog value; when editing, omit it to keep the current value.

groupId.description:
Microsoft Entra ID group ID the deployment is assigned to. `null` when the assignment does not target
a specific group, for example when `targetType` is `AllUsers`, `AllDevices` or
`NotSet`.

groupName.description:
Display name of the assigned group. May be `null`, for example when the assignment does not target a
group or the name could not be resolved.

targetType.description:
Who the assignment targets. `Group` targets the group in `groupId`. `AllUsers` and
`AllDevices` target the whole tenant. `NotSet` means the deployment is assigned to nobody, which
is always the case for the `NoAssignmentsInstall` and `NoAssignmentsUpdate` intents.

intent.description:
What Intune does with the app for this assignment, for example `Required`, `Available`,
`Uninstall` or `UpdateOnly`.

DeploymentAssignmentDto.description: An assignment currently on a deployment: who the deployment targets and with what intent.

displayName.description: Display name of the Intune category.

DeploymentCategoryDto.description: An Intune category assigned to a deployment or deployment template.

additionalArgument.description: Additional command-line arguments passed to the installer, if any.

installLoggingPath.description: Folder path the installation log is written to, if set.

customRequirements.description:
Custom requirement rules currently set on the deployment, such as minimum operating system, hardware, and
file, registry or script rules.

appInfo.description: Overrides for the application information shown in the Company Portal.

conflictingProcess.description:
How the deployment behaves when a conflicting process is running, and which processes count as
conflicting.

returnCodes.description: Installer exit codes and how the deployment interprets each one.

builtInUpdate.description: Whether the application's own built-in updater is enabled, disabled, or not available.

allowAvailableUninstall.description: Whether end users can uninstall the application themselves from the Company Portal.

removeDesktopShortcuts.description: Whether desktop shortcuts created by the installer are removed after installation.

appVersionsRetention.description: Number of previous application versions kept in Intune. `0` means previous versions are not kept.

roleScopeTags.description: Intune role scope tags applied to the deployment.

DeploymentConfigurationDto.description: A deployment's current configuration, returned when you get the details of a single deployment.

additionalArgument.description:
Additional command-line arguments passed to the installer. When omitted on create, no additional
arguments are passed.

installLoggingPath.description: Folder path the installation log is written to. When omitted on create, no log path is set.

customRequirements.description:
Custom requirement rules: minimum operating system, memory, CPU speed and logical processors, excluded
architectures, and file, registry and script rules. When omitted on create, the deployment has no custom
requirements.

appInfo.description:
Overrides for the application information shown in the Company Portal. When omitted on create, nothing is
overridden and the catalog values are used.

conflictingProcess.description:
How the deployment behaves when a conflicting process is running, and which processes count as
conflicting. When omitted on create, the policy is `None`.

returnCodes.description:
Installer exit codes and how the deployment interprets each one. The list replaces any existing return
codes, so send the complete set. When omitted on create, the deployment has no custom return codes.

builtInUpdate.description:
Whether the application's own built-in updater is enabled, disabled, or not available. When omitted on
create, the value is `NotAvailable`. Only meaningful for Patch My PC catalog applications; the
Patch My PC portal does not offer it for custom applications.

allowAvailableUninstall.description:
Whether end users can uninstall the application themselves from the Company Portal. When omitted on
create, the value is `false`.

removeDesktopShortcuts.description:
Whether desktop shortcuts created by the installer are removed after installation. When omitted on
create, the value is `false`.

appVersionsRetention.description:
Number of previous application versions to keep in Intune. `0` means previous versions are not kept.
When omitted on create, the value is `0`.

roleScopeTagIds.description:
IDs of the Intune role scope tags to apply to the deployment. When omitted on create, no scope tags are
applied. There is no endpoint to list scope tags, so get the IDs from the Intune admin center.

DeploymentConfigurationRequest.description:
Optional deployment configuration, used when creating or editing a deployment. Every field is optional.
When creating, an omitted field gets the same default value as a deployment created without this object.
When editing, an omitted field keeps the deployment's current value.

policy.description:
What happens when a conflicting process is running: `None` does nothing, `Kill` closes the
process, `Skip` skips the installation, and `Notify` notifies the user. When omitted on create,
the policy is `None`.

userAddedProcesses.description:
Process names to treat as conflicting, in addition to the application's default list of conflicting
processes.

userDeletedProcesses.description: Process names to remove from the application's default list of conflicting processes.

preventConflictingProcessRestart.description:
Whether a conflicting process that was closed is prevented from restarting after installation. When
`policy` is `Notify` or `Kill` and this is omitted, it defaults to `false`.

postDeploymentNotificationPolicy.description:
Whether the end user is shown a notification after the deployment completes. Must be `DoNotShow` when
`policy` is `None`, or when `policy` is `Skip` with no
`snoozingNotificationDelaySeconds` delay. Other values in those cases are rejected.

snoozingNotificationDelaySeconds.description:
How long, in seconds, the installation is retried silently before the user is notified. `0` means
the user is not notified. Only used when `policy` is `Skip`.

notification.description:
How the end user is notified and how long they can defer. Only used when `policy` is `Notify`.
When `policy` is `Notify` and this is omitted, the Patch My PC portal's default notification
settings are used.

DeploymentConflictingProcessDto.description:
How a deployment behaves when a process that conflicts with the installation is running, and which processes
count as conflicting. On edit, omitted fields keep their current values.

disableArchitectures.description: Processor architectures the deployment does not apply to. Empty when no architecture is excluded.

minimumWindowsOSVersion.description: Minimum Windows version a device must run. `null` when not set.

minimumNumberOfProcessors.description: Minimum number of logical processors a device must have. `null` when not set.

minimumMemoryInMB.description: Minimum amount of system memory a device must have, in MB. `null` when not set.

minimumCpuSpeedInMHz.description: Minimum CPU speed a device must have, in MHz. `null` when not set.

DeploymentCustomRequirementsDto.description:
Custom requirement rules for a deployment or deployment template. A device must meet these requirements
before the application installs on it.

policy.description:
How deferral is limited: unlimited, by a number of deferrals (`Count`), or by a deadline
(`Deadline`).

defaultAction.description: What happens when the notification times out before the user makes a choice.

deferCount.description: Maximum number of times the user can defer. Only used when `policy` is `Count`.

deadline.description: Deferral deadline, in days. Only used when `policy` is `Deadline`.

id.description: ID of the referenced deployment. Same value as `deploymentId`.

deploymentId.description: ID of the referenced deployment. Same value as `id`; prefer this field.

name.description: Display name of the referenced deployment.

iconUrl.description: URL of the icon for the referenced deployment's application.

catalogFeedType.description:
Catalog the referenced deployment's application comes from, for example `PMPC` for the Patch My PC
catalog or `CUSTOMER` for your own custom applications.

DeploymentDependencyDto.description:
A deployment in a dependency chain: a deployment this deployment depends on, a deployment that depends on
it, or a deployment that can be chosen as a new dependency.

productId.description: ID of the application the deployment was created for.

catalogEntryId.description:
The stored AppCat category identifier, available on both list and detail responses.
For public applications this identifies the selected variant; for custom applications it identifies
the customer-owned catalog entry, not its ProductId. Null when the stored identifier is absent.

osType.description: Operating system the deployment targets, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

status.description:
Current status of the deployment, for example `InProgress`, `Success`, `Failed` or
`Retrying`. Create and edit requests return `InProgress` while the change is applied in Intune.

warningMessages.description:
Warnings that did not stop the deployment, for example an ESP profile or role scope tag that could not be
applied. Empty when there are no warnings.

syncOnHold.description:
Whether the deployment's scheduled sync is paused. `true` after you pause it, `false` after you
resume it. New deployments start with `false`.

ringsEnabled.description:
Whether ring-based (phased) deployment is enabled. Ring-enabled deployments are managed in the Patch My PC
portal and cannot be edited through this API.

actions.description:
Operations you can currently perform on this deployment, based on its state. Possible values are
`edit`, `delete`, `redeploy`, `sync`, `pause-sync` and `resume-sync`. This
reflects the deployment's state, not your permissions.

errorMessages.description:
Reasons the deployment last failed. Empty when the deployment has not failed. Check this when
`status` stays at `Retrying`, to find out why the deployment cannot complete.

categories.description: Intune categories assigned to the deployment.

espProfiles.description: Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles assigned to the deployment.

assignments.description:
Assignments currently on the deployment: who it targets and with what intent. Empty, never
`null`, when the deployment has no assignments.

parentDeployments.description: Deployments this deployment depends on. These must finish installing first.

childDeployments.description: Deployments that depend on this deployment.

version.description:
Application version the deployment currently delivers, for example `1.0`. After a sync, this shows
the version the deployment moved to.

configuration.description:
The deployment's current configuration: conflicting-process behavior, return codes, requirements, install
parameters, app information overrides and behavior settings.

DeploymentDetailDto.description:
Full details of a single Intune deployment. Includes everything in the deployment list, plus fields that are
only returned when you get one deployment: error messages, categories, ESP profiles, assignments,
dependencies, version and configuration.

productId.description: ID of the application the deployment was created for.

catalogEntryId.description:
The stored AppCat category identifier, available on both list and detail responses.
For public applications this identifies the selected variant; for custom applications it identifies
the customer-owned catalog entry, not its ProductId. Null when the stored identifier is absent.

osType.description: Operating system the deployment targets, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

status.description:
Current status of the deployment, for example `InProgress`, `Success`, `Failed` or
`Retrying`. Create and edit requests return `InProgress` while the change is applied in Intune.

warningMessages.description:
Warnings that did not stop the deployment, for example an ESP profile or role scope tag that could not be
applied. Empty when there are no warnings.

syncOnHold.description:
Whether the deployment's scheduled sync is paused. `true` after you pause it, `false` after you
resume it. New deployments start with `false`.

ringsEnabled.description:
Whether ring-based (phased) deployment is enabled. Ring-enabled deployments are managed in the Patch My PC
portal and cannot be edited through this API.

actions.description:
Operations you can currently perform on this deployment, based on its state. Possible values are
`edit`, `delete`, `redeploy`, `sync`, `pause-sync` and `resume-sync`. This
reflects the deployment's state, not your permissions.

DeploymentDto.description:
An Intune deployment of an application. Returned when you list deployments, and when you create or edit a
deployment.

displayName.description: Display name of the ESP profile.

applicationsCount.description: Number of applications included in the ESP profile, if known.

DeploymentEspProfileDto.description: An Intune Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profile assigned to a deployment or deployment template.

code.description: Exit code returned by the installer, for example `3010`.

type.description: How the deployment treats `code`, for example as success, failure, retry or reboot required.

DeploymentReturnCodeDto.description:
An installer exit code and how the deployment interprets it. When you set return codes, the list replaces
the existing set, so send every code you need.

id.description: ID of the role scope tag.

displayName.description: Display name of the role scope tag.

DeploymentRoleScopeTagDto.description: An Intune role scope tag applied to a deployment or deployment template.

isDefault.description:
Whether this is the connection's default template. A connection has exactly one default template, and it
cannot be deleted.

osType.description: Operating system the template applies to, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

builtInUpdate.description: Whether the application's own built-in updater is enabled, disabled, or not available.

allowAvailableUninstall.description: Whether end users can uninstall the application themselves from the Company Portal.

removeDesktopShortcuts.description: Whether desktop shortcuts created by the installer are removed after installation.

appVersionsRetention.description: Number of previous application versions kept in Intune. `0` means previous versions are not kept.

customVendor.description: Publisher name shown in the Company Portal instead of the catalog value.

customDeveloper.description: Developer name shown in the Company Portal instead of the catalog value.

customOwner.description: Owner shown in the Company Portal for deployments created from this template.

customNotes.description: Free-text notes shown in the Company Portal for deployments created from this template.

customRequirements.description:
Custom requirement rules applied to deployments created from this template. A device must meet them
before the application installs on it.

categories.description: Intune categories applied to deployments created from this template.

espProfiles.description: Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles applied to deployments created from this template.

roleScopeTags.description: Intune role scope tags applied to deployments created from this template.

copyForwardAssignments.description: Whether a deployment created from this template inherits the template's assignments.

actions.description:
Operations you can currently perform on this template: `edit` and `delete`. The default
template cannot be deleted, so it only offers `edit`.

DeploymentTemplateDto.description: A deployment template and the settings a deployment created from it inherits.

connectionId.description: ID of the Intune connection (tenant) the template belongs to. Required.

osType.description: Operating system the template applies to, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

isDefault.description:
Whether this template becomes the connection's default template. A connection has exactly one default,
so setting this to `true` removes the default status from the current default template.

builtInUpdate.description: Whether the application's own built-in updater is enabled, disabled, or not available.

allowAvailableUninstall.description: Whether end users can uninstall the application themselves from the Company Portal.

removeDesktopShortcuts.description: Whether desktop shortcuts created by the installer are removed after installation.

appVersionsRetention.description: Number of previous application versions to keep in Intune. `0` means previous versions are not kept.

customVendor.description: Publisher name shown in the Company Portal instead of the catalog value.

customDeveloper.description: Developer name shown in the Company Portal instead of the catalog value.

customOwner.description: Owner shown in the Company Portal for deployments created from this template.

customNotes.description: Free-text notes shown in the Company Portal for deployments created from this template.

copyForwardAssignments.description: Whether a deployment created from this template inherits the template's assignments.

categoryIds.description:
IDs of the Intune categories to apply to deployments created from this template. Omit, or send an empty
list, for no categories.

espProfileIds.description:
IDs of the Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profiles to apply to deployments created from this template. Omit,
or send an empty list, for none.

roleScopeTagIds.description:
IDs of the Intune role scope tags to apply to deployments created from this template. Omit, or send an
empty list, for none.

customRequirements.description:
Custom requirement rules to apply to deployments created from this template. Omit for no custom
requirements.

DeploymentTemplateRequest.description:
The settings to store on a deployment template. When updating a template, every field is stored as sent, so
get the template first and change only what you need.

isDefault.description:
Whether this is the connection's default template. A connection has exactly one default template, and it
cannot be deleted.

osType.description: Operating system the template applies to, for example `Windows` or `MacOS`.

createdAt.description: Date and time the template was created.

lastModifiedAt.description: Date and time the template was last modified.

actions.description:
Operations you can currently perform on this template: `edit` and `delete`. The default
template cannot be deleted, so it only offers `edit`.

DeploymentTemplateSummaryDto.description:
A deployment template, as returned in the list of templates for a connection. Get a single template to see
all of its settings.

policy.description: Whether the user can defer the installation, or the conflicting application is closed automatically.

timeOutSeconds.description:
How long, in seconds, the notification is shown before the default action is taken. Must be between
`60` (1 minute) and `82800` (23 hours). The Patch My PC portal default is `300` (5 minutes).

timeOutUseMaxRuntime.description:
Whether the notification timeout follows the deployment's maximum run time instead of
`timeOutSeconds`.

focusAssistPolicy.description: What happens to the notification while Windows Focus Assist is suppressing notifications.

defer.description: How many times, or for how long, the user can defer. Only used when `policy` allows deferral.

DeploymentUserNotificationDto.description:
How the end user is notified when a conflicting process blocks the installation. Used when the
conflicting-process `policy` is `Notify`. On edit, omitted fields keep their current values.

rulesType.description:
The detection method the application uses. `PMPC` detects the application by its MSI product
code, set in `productCodeRule`. `Manual` uses your own file and registry rules, set in
`fileSystemRules` and `registryRules`. `Script` runs the detection script in
`scriptRule`.

productCodeRule.description: MSI product code detection rule. Used when `rulesType` selects MSI product code detection.

scriptRule.description: Script detection rule. An application has at most one detection script.

DetectionRulesDto.description:
Detection rules that determine whether the application is already installed on a device. If you
omit these on a create or update request, detection is based on the request's `msiProductCode`,
`arpDisplayNameMatch` and `arpVersionMatch` fields.

disableArchitectures.description:
Processor architectures the deployment does not apply to. When editing, omit it to keep the current
value.

minimumWindowsOSVersion.description: Minimum Windows version a device must run. When editing, omit it to keep the current value.

minimumNumberOfProcessors.description:
Minimum number of logical processors a device must have. When editing, omit it to keep the current
value.

minimumMemoryInMB.description:
Minimum amount of system memory a device must have, in MB. When editing, omit it to keep the current
value.

minimumCpuSpeedInMHz.description: Minimum CPU speed a device must have, in MHz. When editing, omit it to keep the current value.

fileRules.description:
Complete set of file and folder requirement rules. A list you send, even an empty one, replaces the
existing rules. When editing, omit it to keep the current rules.

registryRules.description:
Complete set of registry requirement rules. A list you send, even an empty one, replaces the existing
rules. When editing, omit it to keep the current rules.

scriptRules.description:
Complete set of script requirement rules. A list you send, even an empty one, replaces the existing
rules. When editing, omit it to keep the current rules.

EditDeploymentCustomRequirementsRequest.description:
Custom requirement rules for a deployment or deployment template. A device must meet these requirements
before the application installs on it. When creating, omit a field to leave that requirement unset. When
editing a deployment, omit a field to keep its current value. A rule list you send, even an empty one,
replaces all existing rules of that type, so send the complete set.

connectionId.description: ID of the Intune connection (tenant) the deployment belongs to. Required.

name.description:
New display name for the deployment. Must not match the name of another deployment in the connection for
the same installer type; a duplicate name returns a 400 response. Omit it to keep the current name.

assignments.description:
Complete set of assignments for the deployment, replacing all existing assignments. Omit it to keep the
current assignments. An empty list is rejected, because a deployment needs at least one assignment.

configuration.description:
Configuration changes to apply: conflicting-process behavior, return codes, requirements, install
parameters, app information overrides and behavior settings. Omit it, or omit any field inside it, to
keep the current value.

categoryIds.description:
Complete set of Intune category IDs, replacing all existing categories. Omit it to keep the current
categories, or send an empty list to remove them all.

espProfileIds.description:
Complete set of Enrollment Status Page (ESP) profile IDs, replacing all existing ESP profiles. Omit it to
keep the current ESP profiles, or send an empty list to remove them all. There is no endpoint to list ESP
profiles, so get the profile ID from the Intune admin center.

parentDeploymentIds.description:
Complete set of IDs of the deployments this deployment depends on, replacing all existing dependencies.
Omit it to keep the current dependencies, or send an empty list to remove them all. Use the dependency
candidates endpoint to find eligible deployments.

EditDeploymentRequest.description:
Request body to edit an existing Intune deployment. The deployment is identified by the `deploymentId`
in the route. All fields except `connectionId` are optional; an omitted field keeps its current value.
Ring-enabled deployments cannot be edited, and settings this request does not include, such as rings, custom
scripts and extra files, are always kept unchanged.

operator.description: How the detected value is compared with `comparisonValue`.

path.description: Full path of the folder that contains the file or folder to check, for example `C:\Program Files\Contoso`.

fileOrFolderName.description: Name of the file or folder to check within `path`.

check32BitOn64System.description: When `true`, checks the 32-bit locations on a 64-bit system.

operationType.description:
What to check about the file or folder, such as whether it exists, its version, its size, or its
created or modified date.

comparisonValue.description:
The value the detected value is compared with. Required when `operationType` compares a value,
such as a version or size.

FileRuleDto.description: A file or folder rule, used as a detection rule or a requirement rule.

operator.description:
How the installed product version is compared with `productVersion`. Applies only when
`productVersion` is set.

productCode.description: The MSI product code (a GUID) that identifies the installed application.

productVersion.description: Optional product version to compare with the installed version, using `operator`.

MsiDetectionRuleDto.description: An MSI product code detection rule.

architectures.description: Architectures available for the requested operating system.

languages.description: Languages available for the requested operating system.

installerTypes.description: Installer types available for the requested operating system.

installContexts.description: Install contexts available for the requested operating system.

PmpcApplicationDetailsDto.description: Details specific to a Patch My PC catalog application. This object has no fields yet.

type.description:
The application type: `pmpc` for a Patch My PC catalog application, `custom` for
one of your custom applications, or `winget` for a Winget application. Treat any other
value as an unknown type.

pmpc.description:
Details specific to a Patch My PC catalog application. Present only when `type` is
`pmpc`.

custom.description: Details specific to a custom application. Present only when `type` is `custom`.

winget.description: Details specific to a Winget application. Present only when `type` is `winget`.

actions.description:
The actions you can currently perform on this application. A custom application allows
`deploy`, `update`, `edit`, `delete` and `download-files`; a Patch
My PC catalog application allows `deploy` only.

language.description: The application's language code, for example `en-US`.

vendorName.description: The name of the application's publisher (vendor).

silentInstallArguments.description:
The command-line arguments used to install the application silently. For an MSI installer,
this is the MSI command line.

mainFile.description: The file name of the application's main installer file.

architecture.description: The processor architecture a device must have to install the application.

installerType.description: The type of installer the application uses, for example `MSI` or `EXE`.

updateVersion.description: The version number of the application's latest version.

installContext.description: The context the application installs in, for example `System` or `User`.

conflictingProcessList.description: The names of processes that conflict with installing the application.

detectionRules.description:
Custom rules that detect whether the application is installed. `null` when none are
set, and always `null` for a Patch My PC catalog application.

customRequirements.description: Custom requirement rules a device must meet before the application installs.

arpDisplayNameMatch.description:
A pattern that matches the application's display name in Add/Remove Programs (ARP), used to
detect whether the application is installed.

msiProductCode.description:
The MSI product code (a GUID) of the application's installer. `null` when the installer
is not an MSI, and always `null` for a Patch My PC catalog application.

iconURL.description:
A reference to the application's icon file. This is a key, not a download link; the icon
image itself is returned in `iconBase64`.

iconBase64.description:
The application's icon image, Base64-encoded. `null` when the application has no icon or
the icon could not be retrieved.

iconContentType.description:
The MIME type of the icon in `iconBase64`, for example `image/png`. Set only when
`iconBase64` is set.

silentUninstallArguments.description: The command-line arguments used to uninstall the application silently.

privacyUrl.description: The URL of the application's privacy policy.

informationUrl.description: The URL of a web page with more information about the application.

intuneNotes.description: Notes to include with the application in Microsoft Intune.

ProductDto.description: Full details of an application, returned by `GET /apps/{productId}`.

vendorIds.description: Return only applications from these publishers, identified by vendor ID.

languages.description: Return only applications in these languages, for example `en-US`.

architectures.description: Return only applications for these processor architectures.

osType.description:
The operating system to search: `Windows` or `MacOS`. Defaults to `Windows`.
macOS results from the Patch My PC catalog are returned only when your account has the macOS
Applications feature; otherwise the search returns no results. Searches of your custom
applications are not affected by this feature.

feedTypes.description:
The catalog feeds to search. Each search endpoint sets this from its route, so any value you
send is ignored: `/apps/search` and `/apps/custom/search` search your custom
applications, and `/apps/public/search` searches the Patch My PC catalog.

connectionId.description:
The ID of the Intune connection that scopes the search. Required when searching the Patch My PC
catalog; not needed when searching your custom applications.

lastModifiedFromUtc.description: The start of the last-modified date range to filter on, in UTC.

lastModifiedToUtc.description: The end of the last-modified date range to filter on, in UTC.

lastUpdatedFromUtc.description: The start of the last-updated date range to filter on, in UTC.

lastUpdatedToUtc.description: The end of the last-updated date range to filter on, in UTC.

displayNameSearchString.description: Text to search for in application display names.

skip.description: Number of matching products to skip before returning the page.

limit.description: Maximum number of matching products to return. Defaults to 50.

sortField.description:
The application property to sort matching results by, such as `DisplayName`.
Defaults to `DisplayName`.

ascending.description: Whether to sort results in ascending order. Defaults to `true`.

includeIconData.description:
Whether to include each application's icon image in `iconBase64` and
`iconContentType`. Defaults to `false`. Including icons makes the search slower.

ProductFilterRequest.description: Search criteria for the application search endpoints. All filters are optional.

totalAmount.description: Total number of products matching the filters, before applying `Skip` and `Limit`.

totalVariantsAmount.description:
The total number of matching application variants across all pages, where one application can
have more than one variant.

products.description: The applications on this page of results.

ProductFilterResponse.description: One page of application search results.

id.description:
The application's ID. Contains the same value as `productId`; use `productId` in new
integrations.

type.description:
The application type: `pmpc` for a Patch My PC catalog application, `custom` for
one of your custom applications, or `winget` for a Winget application. Treat any other
value as an unknown type.

pmpc.description:
Details specific to a Patch My PC catalog application. Present only when `type` is
`pmpc`.

custom.description: Details specific to a custom application. Present only when `type` is `custom`.

winget.description: Details specific to a Winget application. Present only when `type` is `winget`.

actions.description:
The actions you can currently perform on this application. A custom application allows
`deploy`, `update`, `edit`, `delete` and `download-files`; a Patch My
PC catalog application allows `deploy` only.

updateId.description:
Deprecated: a custom application's update identifier, retained for compatibility with existing
clients. Use `custom.updateId` instead.

vendorName.description: The name of the application's publisher (vendor).

language.description: The application's language code, for example `en-US`.

iconURL.description:
A reference to the application's icon file. This is a key, not a download link; to get the
icon image, set `includeIconData` in the search request.

iconBase64.description:
The application's icon image, Base64-encoded. Set only when the search request sets
`includeIconData` to `true` and the icon could be retrieved.

iconContentType.description:
The MIME type of the icon in `iconBase64`, for example `image/png`. Set only when
`iconBase64` is set.

state.description: The current state of the application version.

lastUpdated.description: When the application was last updated, as an ISO 8601 date and time with a UTC offset.

version.description:
The application's latest version number for the searched operating system. An empty string when
no version is available for that operating system. For a Patch My PC catalog application this is
not a specific selectable variant; use the variants in the application details.

one of your custom applications.

itself is returned in `iconBase64`.

The application's icon image, Base64-encoded. `null` when the application has no icon or
the icon could not be retrieved.

iconContentType.description:

`iconBase64` is set.

privacyUrl.description: The URL of the application's privacy policy.

informationUrl.description: The URL of a web page with more information about the application.

intuneNotes.description: Notes to include with the application in Microsoft Intune.

installerType.description: The type of installer the application uses, for example `MSI` or `EXE`.

architecture.description: The processor architecture a device must have to install the application.

installContext.description: The context the application installs in, for example `System` or `User`.

actions.description:
The actions you can currently perform on this application. A custom application allows
`deploy`, `update`, `edit`, `delete` and `download-files`; a Patch My
PC catalog application allows `deploy` only.

variants.description:
Deployable variants for the requested operating system. Each variant contains its own
language, version, installer type, architecture, and install context. Its
pmpc.appcatbroker.api.DTOs.PublicApplicationVariantDto.CatalogEntryId can be supplied as `CatalogEntryId` when
creating a deployment.

PublicApplicationDto.description:
Details of a Patch My PC catalog application, returned by `GET /apps/public/{productId}`.
Patch My PC manages the installation settings for catalog applications, so they are not included.

productId.description: Owning product identifier, retaining context when this variant is selected independently.

catalogEntryId.description: Stable variant identifier, corresponding to the AppCat category ID used when creating a deployment.

osType.description: Operating system this variant can be deployed to.

installerType.description: Installer type used by this variant.

PublicApplicationVariantDto.description: A selectable variant of a public catalog application for a specific operating system.

operator.description: How the detected value is compared with `comparisonValue`.

check32BitOn64System.description: When `true`, checks the 32-bit registry view (WOW6432Node) on a 64-bit system.

keyPath.description: Full path of the registry key to check.

valueName.description: Name of the registry value to check within `keyPath`. Omit to check the key itself.

operationType.description:
What to check about the registry key or value, such as whether it exists, or its string, integer or
version value.

comparisonValue.description:
The value the detected value is compared with. Required when `operationType` compares a value,
such as a string, integer or version.

RegistryRuleDto.description: A registry rule, used as a detection rule or a requirement rule.

operator.description: How the script's output is compared with `comparisonValue`.

displayName.description: Display name for the script rule.

runAsAccount.description:
Set to `true` to run the script as the signed-in user instead of the system account. When
`null`, the default account is used.

comparisonValue.description: The value the script's output is compared with. Required when `operationType` compares a value.

enforceSignatureCheck.description: When `true`, the script must have a valid digital signature before it runs.

runAs32Bit.description: When `true`, the script runs in a 32-bit process on 64-bit systems.

scriptContent.description: The full text of the script to run. Supply the script content, not a path to a script file.

operationType.description: The data type the script's output is read as, such as string, integer, version or boolean.

ScriptRuleDto.description:
A script rule, used as a detection rule or a requirement rule. Detection uses a single script rule;
requirements can include several.

connectionId.description: ID of the Intune connection (tenant) the deployment belongs to. Required.

pause.description: `true` to pause the deployment's scheduled sync, or `false` to resume it.

SetDeploymentSyncPauseRequest.description:
Request body to pause or resume a deployment's scheduled sync. The deployment is identified by the
`deploymentId` in the route.

gatewayJwt.description:
A short-lived access token. Send it as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header of
subsequent API calls until it expires.

expiresIn.description:
Number of seconds until the access token in `gatewayJwt` expires. Exchange your personal access
token again to get a new access token.

TokenExchangeResponse.description:
The access token returned when you exchange a personal access token (PAT). Send this token as a bearer
token in the `Authorization` header of your subsequent API calls.

WingetApplicationDetailsDto.description: Details specific to a Winget application. This object has no fields yet.

bearerAuth.description: An access token from exchanging a personal access token at POST /v1/api/auth/token. Access tokens are valid for 60 minutes.
